items.followUp: Can a hydrometer be used to measure the density of water? Name the instrument specially used to test milk.

rubric.why: Confirms that a hydrometer can measure the density of a liquid such as milk.
rubric.description: States that a hydrometer can measure milk’s density.
rubric.how: Award for a clear yes and reference to measuring density with a hydrometer.

rubric.why: Identifies the specialised hydrometer used for milk.
rubric.description: Names a lactometer as a special hydrometer for milk.
rubric.how: Award for identifying a lactometer or describing it as a hydrometer specially used for milk.

modelAnswer: Yes. A hydrometer can be used to measure the density of milk.
A lactometer is a special type of hydrometer designed for testing milk.

rubric.why: Like forces act in the same direction.
rubric.description: States the direction of like forces.
rubric.how: Award for stating that like forces act in the same direction.

rubric.why: Unlike forces act in opposite directions.
rubric.description: States the direction of unlike forces.
rubric.how: Award for stating that unlike forces act in opposite directions.

modelAnswer: Like forces act in the same direction.
Unlike forces act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: What is a measuring instrument? Describe a measuring tape and state its least count.

rubric.why: Gives the defining purpose of a measuring instrument.
rubric.description: Defines a measuring instrument.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is a device used to measure a physical quantity.

rubric.why: States the meter rod’s length.
rubric.description: Gives the length of a meter rod.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it is one metre (100 cm) long.

rubric.why: Describes the meter rod’s graduations.
rubric.description: States that the meter rod is graduated in centimetres and millimetres.
rubric.how: Award for naming the scale divisions or stating that it is graduated in cm and mm.

rubric.why: Identifies the meter rod’s smallest division, which determines its least count.
rubric.description: Gives the least count and use of the meter rod.
rubric.how: Award for stating that its least count is 1 mm (0.1 cm) or that it measures length to the nearest millimetre.

modelAnswer: Devices used to measure physical quantities are called measuring instruments.
A meter rod is a one-metre-long graduated strip used to measure length.
It is marked in centimetres, with each centimetre divided into millimetres.
Its least count is 1 mm (0.1 cm).

items.followUp: Using a speed–time graph, derive the relation v_f^2-v_i^2=2as.

rubric.why: Uses the slope of the speed–time graph to relate acceleration, time and speeds.
rubric.description: Obtains the acceleration relation from the graph’s slope.
rubric.how: Award for a correct slope relation such as a=(Vf−Vi)/t.

rubric.why: Uses the area under the speed–time graph as displacement.
rubric.description: Expresses displacement as the graph’s area.
rubric.how: Award for the trapezium-area expression for displacement.

rubric.why: Rearranges the acceleration relation for substitution.
rubric.description: Relates time to the change in speed and acceleration.
rubric.how: Award for a correct rearrangement of the slope equation.

rubric.why: Reaches the required kinematic relation.
rubric.description: Derives the required result.
rubric.how: Award for the final relation with the correct terms and signs.

modelAnswer: From the slope of the speed–time graph, a=(V_f−V_i)/t.
The displacement s is the area under the graph: s=½(V_i+V_f)t.
From the slope equation, t=(V_f−V_i)/a.
Substituting in the area equation: 2as=(V_i+V_f)(V_f−V_i).
Using (x+y)(x−y)=x²−y², 2as=V_f²−V_i².

items.followUp: A force of 20 N makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. Find its horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Defines resolution as splitting a force into components that combine to give the original force.
rubric.description: Defines resolution of a force.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a force is split into components whose resultant is the original force.

rubric.why: Recognises the components as mutually perpendicular.
rubric.description: States that the resolved components are perpendicular.
rubric.how: Award for specifying that the components are at right angles to one another.

rubric.why: Gives the horizontal component relation.
rubric.description: States the horizontal component formula.
rubric.how: Award for Fx=F cos θ or an equivalent expression.

rubric.why: Gives the vertical component relation.
rubric.description: States the vertical component formula.
rubric.how: Award for Fy=F sin θ or an equivalent expression.

modelAnswer: Resolving a force means splitting it into component forces whose combined effect is the original force.
For a force F at angle θ to the horizontal, the two components are perpendicular.
The horizontal component is F_x=F cos θ.
The vertical component is F_y=F sin θ.

items.followUp: List four other SI derived units and name the quantities they measure.

rubric.why: A pair of correct derived units earns the first mark.
rubric.description: Lists two valid derived units.
rubric.how: Award for any two distinct correct derived units.

rubric.why: A further pair of correct derived units earns the second mark.
rubric.description: Lists two further valid derived units.
rubric.how: Award for two more distinct correct derived units; together with the first point, four units should be listed.

modelAnswer: Four SI derived units are:
metre per second (m/s), the unit of speed;
metre per second squared (m/s²), the unit of acceleration;
newton (N), the unit of force;
joule (J), the unit of energy or work.

items.followUp: Name four commonly used prefixes and state the power of ten represented by each.

rubric.why: Two correct commonly used prefixes earn the first mark.
rubric.description: Names two valid prefixes.
rubric.how: Award for any two distinct standard prefixes.

rubric.why: Two further correct prefixes earn the second mark.
rubric.description: Names two further valid prefixes.
rubric.how: Award for two more distinct standard prefixes; together with the first point, four prefixes should be named.

modelAnswer: Four commonly used prefixes are kilo (k, 10³),
centi (c, 10⁻²),
milli (m, 10⁻³), and
micro (μ, 10⁻⁶).

items.followUp: What is zero error? Explain how it affects a measurement.

rubric.why: Explains that zero error occurs when an instrument does not read zero for a zero quantity.
rubric.description: Defines zero error.
rubric.how: Award for describing a non-zero instrument reading when the true quantity is zero.

rubric.why: Explains why zero error must be accounted for: to correct the measured value.
rubric.description: States how zero error is used in measurement.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a correction is applied or the reading is adjusted to obtain an accurate measurement.

modelAnswer: Zero error is the non-zero reading shown by an instrument when the quantity being measured is actually zero.
We determine and correct for this error so that the measured value is more accurate.
